input.quote: MarketSite.net Access Fee: Due upon Software Acceptance, and on each annual anniversary of Software Acceptance thereafter.
input.rationale: There is no express take-or-pay, shortfall penalty or user-volume cap on Corio (Software Users are "Unlimited" and the revenue share is transaction/revenue-based; the only "minimum" references are drafting floors and the mutual audit true-up in 4.4). However, the MarketSite.net access fee is a fixed annual charge due on each anniversary (Exhibit B pricing "Year 1 [*] Year 2-5, and beyond: [*]") across a five-year initial term that Corio can only exit for breach or insolvency (11.1/11.2), with no right to reduce or discontinue access. That is effectively a multi-year commitment without an exit, contrary to our position that fees be payable only for services used or ordered. Because the annual access fee is the agreed commercial structure, we take the fallback: a 30 days' notice right to reduce or discontinue MarketSite.net access with a pro-rata true-up rather than a penalty.

proposal.summary: Add a 30-day notice right for Corio to discontinue or reduce MarketSite.net access, with pro-rata true-up instead of continuing annual fees for the full five-year term.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] The MarketSite.net access fee recurs on every anniversary through the five-year initial term with no reduction or discontinuation right, which operates as a take-or-pay commitment. Our position is that fees should be payable only for services actually used or ordered, so we have added a 30 days' notice right to reduce or discontinue access with a pro-rata true-up rather than a penalty.

ops.oldText: MarketSite.net Access Fee: Due upon Software Acceptance, and on each annual anniversary of Software Acceptance thereafter.
ops.newText: MarketSite.net Access Fee: Due upon Software Acceptance, and on each annual anniversary of Software Acceptance thereafter; provided that Corio may discontinue or reduce its MarketSite.net Service access upon thirty (30) days' written notice to Commerce One, in which case no further MarketSite.net Access Fee shall accrue for the discontinued or reduced access and any prepaid fees shall be trued up and refunded on a pro rata basis, without penalty or shortfall charge.
